body:
Ready or not, another week of NFL action is coming in hot and heavy. More than any other year, it does feel like there is a lot to keep up with throughout the league. No matter which way you turn, there are new developments sprouting up, whether it's another international game, injuries, player movement, or hot seats ramping up. It's enough to make anyone's head spin! Fortunately for you, you don't have to keep your head on a swivel with the latest comings and goings across the NFL. Why? Well, you have us! It's our job to make sense of all the madness surrounding the league and package it together for you to easily digest. For the purposes of our little conversation here, we've put together five best bets for Week 7 and handed out picks for every other game on the slate, so when you sit down to watch Sunday's action, you don't have to do too much homework to formulate your wagers. Before the games unfold, check out these last-minute picks for Week 7. Note: Buffalo, Los Angeles (Chargers), Washington, and Jacksonville are on the bye in Week 7.NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.  Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota VikingsSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)We told you last week that the Colts were nowhere near being a 7-point favorite against anyone, including the Titans. That proved to be right on the money as they lost outright, which helped lead to the firing of GM Chris Ballard. I'm not sure if a GM getting fired has the same effect as when a coach gets fired, and you see a galvanized effort the following game. That's especially true when the Indy offense continues to look lost with Daniel Jones at the helm and is now set to face Brian Flores' top-notch Vikings defense. 
This season, Minnesota leads the NFL in blitz rate at a blistering 69.8%. Jones has largely checked down against the blitz this season, with his air yards per attempt falling to 5.2 against the blitz compared to 9.5 without it. In my view, that just means even less of a threat for explosive plays on the Colts' end, which helps keep things in check. The Vikings defense, which will be well rested after being on the bye, is No. 1 in the NFL in third-down and red-zone efficiency. That's a nightmare matchup for the Colts' offense, which is averaging just 4.7 yards per play. Meanwhile, I'm encouraged by Kyler Murray as he's coming off his best performance of the season in Week 5. So far, his passer rating and yards per attempt have improved in each game. With the rest and home-field advantage, Minnesota should leave Indy in the dust. Projected score: Vikings 33, Colts 19The pick: Vikings -6.5Miami Dolphins at New York JetsSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)Sure, the Jets burned us last week, but that shouldn't mean we look at them any differently in Week 7, especially with a fantastic matchup against the winless Dolphins. New York was competitive with the Patriots last week, and they've been a team we've backed several times already in 2026.  
The offense is a concern, as they have the worst red-zone efficiency (38%) in the NFL and rank 27th in points per game (18.7). However, I'm not sure how much that'll matter against a Dolphins offense tied for the fewest points in the NFL (14.0). New York is allowing just 20.3 points per game this season, which is tied for the seventh-fewest in the league. So, it might not be too heavy a lift for Geno Smith and company to jump out in front of the Dolphins and clear the number. Projected score: Jets 23, Dolphins 16The pick: Jets -4.5Cleveland Browns at Tennessee TitansSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)Tennessee notched its first win of the season last week by taking down the Colts, but I don't think this is a sign the Titans are about to crawl out of the basement. The Titans have made incremental improvements, but they were outgained by 213 yards last week despite the win. As I wrote in last week's picks column, taking the Titans to cover was more about Indianapolis than anything else, and that remains true, which is why we're fading them this time around. The Browns are ... good? They pulled off an upset win over the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens last week and, remarkably, stand in first place in the AFC North heading into Week 7. Deshaun Watson has been clutch this season, as he has four game-winning drives where he's been money. In that window, Watson has completed 75% of his passes (18-of-24), thrown for 179 yards, and has two touchdowns with zero interceptions. To his credit, Cam Ward has also popped in the fourth quarter this season as well, but Tennessee is also tied for the fewest points scored in the NFL over the first three quarters. If that persists, Cleveland has a defense capable of snuffing out any late Ward comeback attempt. 
Projected score: Browns 24, Titans 17The pick: Browns -2.5Denver Broncos at Arizona CardinalsSunday, 4:05 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)The Broncos offense is broken. More specifically, Bo Nix appears to be broken. Yeah, they beat the Seahawks last week, but they did that in spite of their quarterback play. Nix averages 5.6 yards per attempt, along with just 4.9 air yards. That air yards per attempt average is the shortest through six games in the past 20 seasons. Overall, the offense is 26th in points per game and 31st in total yards per game and yards per play. Nothing about that screams road favorite. Arizona is coming off its second upset win of the season, slaying the Rams with a strong defensive effort. The Cardinals just held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 16 points. If that even remotely carries over, it's going to be another quiet showing for the Denver offense. Of course, there are concerns about the Cardinals' offense, especially after going 0-5 in the red zone last week, but I have way more faith in that unit than what the Broncos are producing currently. I'll take the points and sprinkle on another upset. Projected score: Cardinals 23, Broncos 20The pick: Cardinals +4.5Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore RavensSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)There's still no official word on whether Lamar Jackson (ankle) will, in fact, return for this game, but he did practice in a limited fashion all week. Even assuming that No. 8 will be under center for Baltimore, I like the Bengals here as they are fresh off a bye in Week 6. Joe Burrow doesn't have the best head-to-head splits against Jackson, but the Bengals QB was playing well entering the break and currently ranks second in completion percentage and seventh in passing yards per game. 
I also believe this week's game will highlight Cincinnati's interior defensive line and expose a weakness in Baltimore's interior offensive line. The Bengals have the second-most sacks in the NFL by defensive tackles through Week 6, while the Ravens have had a rotating door at center. This game could be one of the key examples as to why Cincinnati traded for Dexter Lawrence this offseason. The Bengals are also 10-3 ATS in their last 13 road games after a win that Burrow starts. Projected score: Bengals 30, Ravens 23The pick: Bengals -1.5Rest of the bunchSteelers at Saints (in Paris)Projected score: Steelers 30, Saints 23The pick: Steelers -3

title: Paolo Banchero is hurt again, and this Magic experiment might be cursed - CBS Sports
description: Banchero is reportedly out 4-to-6 weeks with a high ankle sprain
body:
Banchero is reportedly out 4-to-6 weeks with a high ankle sprain
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2024 playoffs were supposed to be the start of something special in Orlando. The Magic had drafted Jalen Suggs, Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero in three straight lotteries and had just pushed Donovan Mitchell and the Cavaliers to seven games. They were young, talented, and when they went all in on the Desmond Bane trade last summer, just about everyone officially stamped them as an Eastern Conference contender. Unfortunately, we've never fully gotten to see what this team could be, and it's starting to look like we never will. Injuries continue to hit them as hard as any team in the NBA. Two games into the 2026-27 season, it's Banchero reportedly headed for a four-to-six week hiatus after suffering a high ankle sprain in Orlando's loss to the Timberwolves on Friday. The Magic just cannot catch a break. Over the last two seasons, the Banchero-Wagner-Suggs trio has managed to play in just 25 games together. Last year, Wagner and Suggs missed a combined 73 games to injury. The year before that, Banchero and Wagner managed just 40 games together. They literally suffered the same injury that year. Banchero tore his oblique in the first week of the season, missed 34 games, and just as he was gearing up to come back, Wagner tore his oblique and missed the next six weeks. 
It's all the more frustrating given the glimpses of actual magic we've seen from this team at full strength. They had the No. 1-seed Pistons down 3-1 in the first round last year until Wagner, of course, missed the last three games of the series with a calf strain and Detroit rallied to win the series. This season, you figured, or hoped, that the needle of injury luck would finally swing in their favor. But here we go again with Banchero, who was off to a roaring start this year with 35 points in the opener and another 14 through the first half on Friday. He was shooting almost 70% from the field. He made three of his four 3-pointers against Atlanta. Aside from the injuries, there have been real questions as to whether Banchero and Wagner can ultimately fit as a duo given both of their shooting inconsistencies. We need to see them together for longer stretches to see if they can make it work, or if Banchero's shooting can improve. The basketball gods just won't let the experiment get off the ground for any real length of time. 
It's too bad, because when Banchero is cooking, he's as lethal a scorer as there is in the league. The Magic can create a lot of inverted mismatches with Banchero's and Wagner's ability to handle the ball and initiate offense at 6-foot-10. Orlando's defense is elite; it had Detroit in a straitjacket for much of that series last year. The pieces are there. But this Banchero injury might seal the fate of this season before it even starts. That sounds premature, but the Magic are already 0-2, and without Banchero for potentially a month and a half, they're very likely going to have to dig out of another deep hole to even think about competing for a playoff spot in the extremely deep East. Truth be told, they were going to have an uphill battle even had they stayed healthy. Now all they can do is hold on as tightly as possible and pray to the basketball gods that nobody else gets hurt before Banchero comes back. The same basketball gods that have seemingly put a curse on a team that might be nearing its end without ever really having had the chance to get started. 
Again, that sounds dramatic. But this feels like a make-or-break year for the Banchero-Wagner duo. The Magic lack the future equity to make another big move. Moving off one of these two is the only real shakeup available. The Magic tried switching coaches, but that's not going to make Banchero or Wagner shoot better and it's not going to make them stay healthy. This was the last shot to really see if this duo can work, and it could not have gotten off to a worse start.

title: Mavericks star Cooper Flagg sprains shoulder on flagrant foul by Pacers' Aaron Nesmith - CBS Sports
description: The reigning NBA Rookie of the Year hurt his shoulder, and the Mavericks got into with Nesmith on Friday night
body:
The reigning NBA Rookie of the Year hurt his shoulder, and the Mavericks got into with Nesmith on Friday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Cooper Flagg, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, left the Dallas Mavericks' 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday with a left shoulder injury just before halftime after being on the receiving end of a flagrant foul by Aaron Nesmith. On Saturday, the Mavs said an MRI revealed a sprained left shoulder for Flagg. He will be reevaluated next week. Mavericks coach Dusty May said that Flagg was in "good spirits" in the locker room, but will be evaluated in the "next couple of days." The Mavericks are set to host the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday before going back on the road to face the Miami Heat on Monday. It appears he'll miss both of those games.
With a minute to play in the first half in Indianapolis, Flagg got a steal and took off the other way on a fast break. It seemed he would have an easy dunk until Nesmith raced in from behind and sent him sprawling with a hard foul. Flagg immediately grabbed for his shoulder, while Mavericks forward Naji Marshall confronted Nesmith under the basket, which led to a big scrum involving players from both teams. Here's a look at the play:
After a review, the foul was upgraded to a Flagrant 1 on Nesmith, and Marshall and Nesmith both received technicals. Flagg made both of his free throws before leaving the game for good. 
"Nesmith's a great guy. Heck of a player. I've known him since he was in high school. An unfortunate play. Hopefully Coop's fine, but obviously it's something we wish wouldn't have happened," May said. 
After putting up 24 points in the win, Kyrie Irving explained why the Mavericks were so quick to stand up for Flagg. "We've got to set an example for every single one of us, especially Coop, our youngest guy on the team. We gotta protect him, and when we see him go down like that, it doesn't make us feel good," Irving said. "That's NBA basketball, it's a brotherhood you create within that locker room. You can see the difference when teams don't show up for each other and we don't want to be one of those teams, so when anyone goes down, especially Coop or myself or anybody, we gotta have each other's back, and we're a family out here and that's the atmosphere we gotta create."Flagg averaged 21 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals last season, and was off to a stellar start in his sophomore campaign. He poured in 32 points on 10 of 17 from the field in the Mavericks' season-opening loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday and had 14 points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals on 4 of 6 shooting in 17 minutes on Friday before he was injured. 
After his stellar rookie season, Flagg checked in at No. 25 on CBS Sports' Top 100 NBA players ranking, which was released earlier this month.

title: Cincinnati stuns Texas Tech: How upset affects Big 12 CFP picture after Reds Raiders loss - CBS Sports
description: The Bearcats just tossed a wrench in the conference's plans for three CFP selections
body:
The Bearcats just tossed a wrench in the conference's plans for three CFP selections

        Down goes another one of college football's remaining unbeatens, this time in the Big 12.Cincinnati's stunning 37-24 win over eighth-ranked Texas Tech on Saturday snapped the Red Raiders' nine-game Big 12 winning streak dating back to last season and threatens the league's shot at three selections in the College Football Playoff.With five top-25 teams entering Week 8, the attention now turns to the primetime battle between 14th-ranked Houston and No. 10 Utah, with the winner getting a leg up on the rest alongside second-ranked BYU at the top of the conference.Behind four touchdown passes from JC French and a career-best 173 yards rushing from Cole Tabb, the Bearcats snapped a two-game skid with a signature win and took advantage of Texas Tech's season-long sputters in the passing game. 
Struggles offensively finally came back to haunt the Red Raiders, who turned it over three times and never recovered from Cincinnati's 21-point surge in the second quarter.The ranked win was only Scott Satterfield's second at Cincinnati in four seasons.It was personal for the Bearcats, who watched last season's starting quarterback Brendan Sorsby leave this offseason sign with Texas Tech out of the transfer portal -- though he never played a down for the Red Raiders. Sorsby was suspended following a gambling investigation before mutually parting ways with Texas Tech in June.
Now, Will Hammond and the Red Raiders' offense must likely win out — with Arizona looming among others — to have a chance at repeating as Big 12 champions to secure an auto-berth into the CFP.Top of Big 12 standingsRankTeamOverall RecordConference RecordNo. 2BYU6-03-0No. 10Utah6-03-0No. 8Texas Tech6-13-1No. 14Houston6-13-1No. 25Arizona5-12-1*BYU is playing at UCF in Week 8 following last weekend's win over Notre Dame, while Houston-Utah play Saturday night and Arizona hosts Iowa State.It's imperative the Big 12's best don't bloody each other up over the second half of the season if this league wants multiple teams in the CFP. The selection committee's new conference strength metric helps contextualize league schedules, including disparities between teams playing slates of varied difficulty.However, only one of the league's five ranked teams in Week 8 has a strength of schedule ranked inside the top-35 nationally, and that's going to be part of the discussion when the CFP selection committee meets next weekend. BYU's currently No. 1 in strength of record and No. 7 in game controls, metrics that will come in handy if Kalani Sitake's team keeps it up as the league favorite.Utah has similar numbers, but the Utes' strength of schedule at No. 99 is worst in the conference.No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah's significanceSaturday night's late game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City provides another glimpse into the league title race exiting Week 8, especially if the Utes can stay undefeated against the Cougars. Houston's won four straight games since an early season loss at Texas Tech and would move into a multi-team tie for second in the conference behind second-ranked BYU with a victory.A Utah win gives the Utes the upper hand in the Big 12 conversation ahead of next week's showdown at Cincinnati before the Nov. 7 showdown with BYU. From Texas Tech's perspective, the best the Red Raiders can finish is 11-1 overall, and from there, the CFP situation gets interesting for Joey McGuire's team.They'll own the head-to-head advantage over Houston in the event the Cougars end up with a single conference loss, but the league goes to tiebreakers with common opponents if Utah or BYU are the teams tied with Texas Tech at the end of the regular season. Cincinnati plays Utah and Houston back-to-back weeks coming up, so the Bearcats will have a say.As you can see, the unpredictable Big 12 and its quest to produce multiple playoff teams this season will be decided over the next few weekends, and Texas Tech's loss on Saturday significantly threatens any shot at getting three teams in the final bracket.

title: Texas Tech's Big 12 hopes hinge on solving the Brendan Sorsby-sized hole at QB - CBS Sports
description: Two costly turnovers and persistent red-zone struggles from Will Hammond in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati exposed
body:
Two costly turnovers and persistent red-zone struggles from Will Hammond in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati exposed a glaring offensive void after Sorsby's sudden departure
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Late in the first half against Cincinnati, No. 8 Texas Tech faced a vital moment. The Red Raiders allowed a touchdown to go down 11 points, but had a prime opportunity to erase the lead in an instant. The Red Raiders faced a two-minute drill and would start the second half with the ball. Quarterback Will Hammond dropped back and made a horrendous read, throwing only two yards downfield toward his checkdown, nearly throwing an interception. After two successful run plays that ran the clock down to 31 seconds, Hammond launched a floating jump ball, calmly intercepted by Cincinnati safety MJ Cannon, setting up a touchdown to end the half that made it a three-score game. Cincinnati had this game circled on the calendar after the dramatic Brendan Sorsby saga over the offseason. In a 37-18 loss, a miserable performance for Hammond, the Red Raiders revealed just how much they miss the portal quarterback, who was forced to step away amidst a gambling probe. To turn back the clock, Sorsby played two seasons at Cincinnati, compiling 5,600 yards before entering the transfer portal. Cincinnati sued him over an alleged unpaid buyout. Then he admitted to placing thousands of dollars in bets, resulting in permanent ineligibility from the NCAA. After a dramatic court ruling restored Sorsby's eligibility, outside pressure forced him to step away. 
Without Sorsby, Texas Tech's staff expressed great confidence in Hammond, who is only now one year removed from a torn ACL. But in the miserable loss to Cincinnati, all of the greatest concerns about Hammond came to fruition. 
        
            
                Cincinnati's upset win over Texas Tech throttles College Football Playoff picture in Big 12
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Hammond's inconsistencyHammond threw for only 227 yards on 37 pass attempts with both an interception and a fumble to boot. The Bearcats scored off both turnovers to build an 18-point halftime lead. During a game-deciding second quarter, Hammond was 2 of 6 for 12 yards with the pick. Cincinnati went on a 21-0 run over the same period. Hammond's inconsistency in the red zone proved especially damaging. He completed only 2 of 6 passes in the red zone, with a sack taken as the Red Raiders failed to score a touchdown on their first three red zone trips. Their first touchdown of the game with less than a minute remaining. 
Through the first three quarters, Hammond had one total completion go for more than 15 yards. More than half of his passing yards -- and only successful shots downfield -- came in the fourth quarter with the game already decided.  And let's be clear, there were plenty of deficiencies shown in the stunning loss. Texas Tech allowed 257 yards on the ground, including a career-high 173 yards to Cincinnati running back Cole Tabb. Last season, the Red Raiders led the Big 12 in rushing defense. The new wave of transfers has not lived up to the standard. Texas Tech's offensive line has also played poorly, despite returning three high-quality starters. They've cycled through three talented running backs, struggling to find a rotation that makes sense. At the same time, opponents are realizing they can stack the box with a quarterback who doesn't scare them. 
There aren't necessarily obvious answers on the roster. Backup Tommy Castellanos started several games in the ACC, but has been embroiled in eligibility cases. He also is an inconsistent passer, completing only 58% of his attempts in his career. Underclassmen Lloyd Jones and Stephen Cannon haven't played much ball. Texas Tech still has a quality win over No. 14 Houston and an important stretch ahead. The Red Raiders host No. 25 Arizona next week before traveling to Oklahoma State in two weeks. The pathway is there for Texas Tech to get back into the Big 12 and College Football Playoff race. Seven games into the season, there is a Brendan Sorsby-shaped hole on the roster. Hammond doesn't look ready to fill it.

title: Aaron Rodgers, Kenneth Walker III address Eagles' handling of Jalen Hurts blood clot situation: 'That's crazy' - CBS Sports
description: Hurts is presumed to miss the rest of the 2026 regular season
body:
Hurts is presumed to miss the rest of the 2026 regular season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jalen Hurts being ruled out indefinitely after blood clots were found in his lungs has drawn reaction from across the NFL. The Philadelphia Eagles have been put under scrutiny for the handling of Hurts' medical issue, specifically in the lead-up to their Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. At the time, a superficial blood clot had been found in Hurts' calf following a team walk-through. Hurts ended up playing in that game before taking the team flight back to the United States. Upon their return stateside and further testing, Hurts was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, which have put him on the shelf for what is believed to be the rest of the regular season. The NFL concluded that the process that led to Hurts playing in Week 5 "was handled appropriately." However, the NFLPA has called for a further investigation into the matter. As for the players themselves, two of the league's most notable players have reacted to what has transpired with Hurts. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has first-person experience with what Hurts is going through after dealing with blood clots in his lungs in high school. 
"Yeah, honestly, just stay positive," Walker said during his Friday press conference. "You know, obviously, I guess you know about what happened in high school, like, with the blood clots and everything.  And he went on the flight, huh, and everything? Yeah, that's crazy. You know, honestly, just stay positive, and, you know, do all the things necessary that he needs to do, like, to get his body back right. But, yeah, I'll be praying for him, because that's not something, you know, we should take lightly."Walker's concern for Hurts being on a flight in his condition has been a common one throughout the NFL, and a legitimate question in the team's handling of the situation. When asked about Hurts on Friday, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who has had disputes with the NFL's medical staff in the past, admitted that he wasn't surprised by the confusing handling of the Eagles signal-caller. "We're in the quarterback fraternity, so you don't want to see anything like that happen to anybody. Especially a guy who's still in football," Rodgers said during his Friday presser. "I don't know all the details about what's going on. All I've seen is what's been printed. Allen Sills, he's the guy in charge of all things medical at the NFL office, and he and I haven't always seen eye-to-eye about things. So, I can't say I'm real surprised."
In a response to the NFLPA's request, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he welcomes an investigation into the handling of Hurts' blood clots but said that "the protocols were followed." "The most important thing here is Jalen's health, ultimately, and the future of him," Goodell said. "He's a wonderful young man; not just a great player, but he's someone we all care deeply about. I'm more worried about his health, ultimately, but the protocols were followed."With Hurts sidelined, Philadelphia has turned to backup quarterback Tanner McKee.

body:
Miami hadn't played as No. 1 in 24 years, and with its play and uniforms, 'The U' looked the part in its destruction of Pitt

        Saturday's showdown between No. 1 Miami and Pittsburgh was not a normal occurrence, even though the two schools have a long-running history across multiple conferences. No, Saturday marked the first time since 2002 that Miami played a game as the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 poll. For 24 years, Miami has been working to get back to the position it held near the end of its magical run through the early 2000s, and Saturday was the first time the Hurricanes could put their newly-minted No. 1 status to the test. Tensions have been tight, too, with No. 1 losing in back-to-back weeks. First, Texas lost to Oklahoma, then Georgia lost to Auburn, and now it's opened the door for the Hurricanes, who survived an upset scare against rival Florida State last week, to move up into the top spot. But the way Miami performed in a 29-point rout of the Panthers quickly put to bed the idea that No. 1 would be changing hands again after Week 8. The Hurricanes were up 17-0 early and leading 31-7 at halftime, dropping three touchdowns after halftime for extra aesthetics on the 52-23 win. 
Miami's best players lived up to their billing, with Darian Mensah throwing for 387 yards on 31-of-37 passing with four touchdowns and Malachi Toney serving as the receiver for 16 catches on 17 targets for 194 yards and three of those scores. If Miami's ascent to No. 1 brought more attention, there wasn't much from Saturday's win that suggested the Hurricanes are anything but. It's yet another marker of success for Mario Cristobal, leading his alma mater back to the ranks of national title contenders that he experienced as a player. Fans yearned for years for "The U" to be "back," but too often over the last 20 years, talented teams fell short. The kind of success the Hurricanes are enjoying now feels sustainable in a way we haven't seen since they were the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 poll.  And while 2002 was the most recent time Miami was No. 1, Saturday was also special because it was a day Miami chose to honor the 2001 national championship team. 
Mensah and Toney spoke after the game about what it meant to have the program's legends around this year's team, with Mensah pointing out that it was not only "motivating" but also a great opportunity to soak up their football knowledge. Toney mentioned connecting with Andre Johnson and Ed Reed, providing plenty of fun for those seeking even more threads to the last time Miami ran college football. Speaking of threads, the nostalgia hit even harder when Miami wore throwback uniforms honoring the 2001 national champions. The orange throwback uniforms over white pants with a white helmet were described by the school as a "legendary look," and it helped that the team put together a final score that would have fit right in with the dominant wins of that title team. "They inspired so many future Hurricanes that end up coming here to the University of Miami. Glad to be able to honor them as well, with a victory," Cristobal said of the 2001 team after the game. "They mean a lot to our guys. I think the best thing that's been happening with our program is within our community and the University of Miami alum community, is that we built some really strong equity, so now those guys are becoming our best advocates, which in turn helps the entire organization become more galvanized."

        
            
                2026 CBS Sports Midseason All-America team: Big Ten edges out SEC, ACC for most selections at halfway point
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Miami stars have chance to join esteemed legacyOne of the great college football parlor games is to start naming some guys, or specifically rolling through the stellar collection of talent that early 2000s Miami had on the roster. Miami wasn't revolving around one individual star; it was a team that offered a candidate to be the very best at his position at nearly every position on the field. It's starting to feel that way again with the 2026 Hurricanes, thanks to the addition of Mensah and the continued development of Toney. Mensah seems to be raising the bar for the QB1 role at Miami, which has become a bit of a glamour position in college football. Two years ago, Cam Ward had the production but fell a couple of wins short of their ceiling, while last season Carson Beck led a playoff run, providing key conversions against one of the best defenses in the country. Mensah seems to be delivering Ward's production with Beck's playoff potential, and his play on its own stands out as the best among quarterbacks in the country. 
When we polled our experts for the Midseason All-America team earlier this week, all but one chose Mensah as their first team quarterback. He had a pretty easy case coming into the weekend as the nation's leader in passer rating, yards per attempt and completion percentage while leading the nation's highest-scoring offense. Trinidad Chambliss, CJ Carr and others will certainly have opportunities to jump Mensah before the end of the season, but if the season ended today, then Miami has the best quarterback in the country.  Toney also finished as the Midseason All-America pick at the all-purpose position, but he's also starting to make his own push for a claim to the crown at wide receiver. Toney's explosiveness was on full display on Saturday at Pitt, with 132 of his 194 receiving yards coming after the catch, providing some truly outstanding moments in the blowout win.Outstanding is a perfect way to describe how Mensah and Toney have looked this season, and it's how we have seen them both ride Miami's success to a spot in the Heisman Trophy race. With just six weeks left until the ballots are due, Mensah and Toney have both played well enough individually to be slotted among the top handful of names on the oddsmakers' board to win the award, which is given to the most outstanding player in college football. 
It's shaping up to be one of those years when the 2026 Hurricanes could end up being a parlor game of their own, with people remembering how amazing it was that Mensah was throwing passes to Toney or that Mark Fletcher Jr. shared a running back room with Javian Mallory. Only the weeks ahead will determine whether this year's Miami team will leave a legacy worthy of nostalgia. Because now that "The U" is back, the expectation for a nostalgia-worthy legacy includes at least one, if not multiple, trophies. Tough tests lie in the weeks aheadSo what's ahead for this rock star crew of ACC heavyweights? First, a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina, which should provide quite the scene under the lights on Halloween. As long as Miami can avoid a spooky lookahead spot in primetime, it will move on to one of the games of the year in college football against Notre Dame in South Bend.  Miami's ability to handle its business on Saturday against Pitt was a positive sign that this team is not going to be prone to the lookahead or letdown spot after an emotional rivalry win against Florida State. Because it would be tempting to look ahead to the best measuring stick game that Miami will get throughout its regular season schedule. 
Miami wants to make another run at the national championship game, and to do that, it will need to beat multiple College Football Playoff teams. So far, the Hurricanes have been laying waste to teams that, other than Wake Forest, are not College Football Playoff contenders. Notre Dame is not just that; it's a national title contender, and that Nov. 7 collision in South Bend is going to set up an electric modern chapter to a recently revived rivalry. After the Notre Dame, win or lose, Miami will again be challenged to manage the fallout and stay in rhythm performing at a high level. The Hurricanes round out their regular season schedule with three straight home games against ACC foes, which is quite the decompression period after a massive win, a heart-breaking loss or anything in between. From there, it will be time to perform in the games that determine whether the 2026 Miami Hurricanes will also be remembered like the players who wore the throwback uniforms on display. The expectation is excellence, and anything less could get exposed as a cheap nostalgia hit. Anything less, and Miami won't find itself at the No. 1 spot much longer. 
The great key about having Cristobal as the head coach of this program's resurgence is that he, as well as perhaps anyone in the world, knows what it needs to look like. If there's anyone policing the standard around this newly crowned king of college football, it's going to be their alumni head coach who was built for this moment.

        Petr Yan had to dig deep in his bantamweight championship defense against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333, but he was able to put on one of the most impressive performances of his career to win a rubber match over the former champion.Dvalishvili won their first meeting in 2023 before going on to claim the title Yan had previously held. Yan kicked off his second reign as champion this past December, avenging that loss with a decision win over Dvalishvili.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of UFC 333, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!Dvalishvili, being a notably faster starter than Yan, brought an expected high-energy approach to the start of the fight. Dvalishvili came out firing big right hands and pushing for takedowns, though Yan capably fended off the takedown attempts to keep the fight standing, and quickly got to his feet in the moments when Dvalishvili was able to finish a takedown attempt. Despite Yan's strong grappling defense, Dvalishvili's constant movement and attack put Yan in a position where he was unable to use his own offensive tools.
Yan landed some hard punches in the early stages of the second round, but Dvalishvili's pace continued to dictate the action, and he was able to get inside and work for takedowns, putting constant pressure on Yan, even when Yan was able to fend off the takedown attempts. Yan's moments were coming in spurts while Dvalishvili was keeping the faucet all the way open.
While things looked as though they'd continue to play out as they had been early in the third round, Yan went back to a tool that had worked well in the rematch, a hard left kick to the body that sent Dvalishvili stumbling backward grabbing at his liver. Dvalishvili recovered, but Yan finished the third having suddenly found success with repeated striking combinations.Yan continued to build on that momentum in Round 4, bringing a constant stream of slick boxing to land to Dvalishvili's head and body. The shots to the body especially seemed to bother Dvalishvili, and Yan was also consistent in fending off Dvalishvili's increasingly desperate takedown attempts.
Despite Dvalishvili's legendary motor and cardio, Yan appeared to be the fresher fighter in the final round, and he used that energy to continue putting big strikes on Dvalishvili.The question at the end of five rounds was who took the third round on the official scorecards. Dvailishvili clearly won the first half of the fight, and the third round, but was Yan's big momentum-turning moment with the body kick in Round 3 enough to retain the title? From that kick onward, the fight had been entirely Yan's.When the official scorecards were read, all three judges saw the fight 48-47 for Yan, winning him the rivalry with an incredible performance where he outlasted and outthought Dvalishvili.
Speaking through an interpreter after the fight, Yan made it clear he knew he could not afford to take his foot off the gas when the fight was entering it's final stages."I was listening to my coach," Yan said. "And he said, 'Look, we're going to the fifth round, and it's two-two. You win the round, you win the fight.'"

His calls for a title shot were impossible to ignore after he avenged his loss to decorated Japanese star Kyoji Horiguchi this summer.Prates and Morales were the top two candidates to challenge welterweight champion Islam Makhachev. It turned out that the brief bit of wrestling from Pico was enough to get Keita to leave himself open on the feet.A sharp Pico right hand put Keita on rubber legs and signaled the beginning of the end. Pico pounced on his damaged opponent, followed him to the canvas and dropped punches until the referee was forced to call a halt to the action just 1:14 after the opening bell.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of UFC 333, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!The win was Pico's second after a disastrous UFC debut. "If you're asking me what I want, I want to fight for a title. But if that can't happen, I want a rematch with Lerone Murphy," Pico said. "All these guys that are sitting on their ranking, not wanting to accept fights, backing out of fights, they need to be benched for a year. It's crazy. I call them rankings squatters.         Arch Manning grew up with the unique culture of Ole Miss all around him. His uncle, Eli Manning, had his jersey retired in Oxford, as was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State.  He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma, and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons, who has a high ankle sprain. 
No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has redisovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week.  Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation: Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season.  "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. 
Life without Colin Simmons: Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%).  Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida: The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home: Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards.

History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight.

        Lone'er Kavanagh redeemed his flyweight hype.After a recent setback slowed his roll, flyweight contender Lone'er Kavanagh very much looked like a serious player at 125 pounds on Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. Kavanagh (11-2), who was submitted by Brandon Royval just three months ago for his second stoppage loss in three fights, bounced back in a major way with a first-round knockout of a dangerous Ramazan Temirov (20-4) in the featured bout inside Etihad Arena. A 27-year-old native of London, Kavanagh has shown flashes of brilliance in five walks to the Octagon entering the Temirov fight, which included a short-notice, five-round decision win at elevation in Mexico City against former champion Brandon Moreno in February that quickly erased the second-round knockout he had suffered against Charles Johnson in his previous fight. Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of UFC 333, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!
But despite his up-and-down nature of late, Kavanagh put it all together in a systematic breakdown of Temirov, a 29-year-old native of Uzbekistan, who entered having won all three UFC starts while riding a 12-fight win streak overall. Temirov, who knocked out former title challenger Steve Erceg in one round in July, came out head hunting early with his explosive power. But Kavanagh never ran from the danger and relied on his speed, footwork, defense and technique to pick him apart. 
A beautiful left uppercut late in Round 1 rocked Temirov and Kavanagh uncorked a lightning quick combination to floor him. Just as Temirov tried to rise to his feet, Kavanagh met him with another uppercut to drop him into the cage and down again as referee Mike Beltran leaped in to stop the fight at 4:28. 
"I have an amazing team behind me and we work hard, day in and day out, to get these results. We trusted in the plan and we got it done," Kavanagh said. "We learned from previous mistakes and one of those was to keep your hands up. So, I made sure I kept my hands up and I made sure I could counter."Kavanagh, who entered as the No. 6-ranked flyweight in the UFC, didn't hide his intentions for the future after the win."Obviously, I'm here for that belt," Kavanagh said. "Respectfully, anyone can get it. I'm here for that belt."

body:
As we get ready for Sunday's slate, there is no shortage of injury news for the Week 7 games. This week, there are some major potential returns and some key players sidelined.Two of the biggest returns we could see this week involve quarterbacks. Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) is questionable and is looking to make his first appearance since Sept. 27. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is out after initially saying he was trending in the right direction to play in the divisional game against the Bengals.Here's a look at game designations for all of Sunday's matchups:Steelers (-3.5) vs. SaintsSteelers: WR Ben Skowronek (calf), CB Brandin Echols (hamstring) OUT; RB Rico Dowdle (knee), S DeShon Elliott (knee) QUESTIONABLESaints: G Cesar Ruiz (knee), DT Nathan Shepherd (illness) QUESTIONABLEThe Steelers and Saints are in France this week, playing at Stade de France just outside of Paris. Steelers S DeShon Elliott (knee) is in his 21-day window to return, and with a full week of full participation in practice, a return feels possible. RB Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in practice all week. T.J. Watt (calf) showed up on the injury report and increased his workload from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. Head coach Mike McCarthy said he wasn't concerned about his star LB's status.Over on the Saints side, just two players are listed on Friday's injury report. G Cesar Ruiz is officially questionable and was able to practice on a limited basis after not participating earlier in the week. If he is unable to play, rookie Jeremiah Wright could be put in his place. DT Nathan Shepherd has missed the last two games. Head coach Kellen Moore would not give details on Shepherd, who didn't practice Friday after practicing all week. RB Alvin Kamara, who was limited all week with a back injury, has no game designation.
49ers (-3.5) vs. Falcons49ers: WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf), LB Luke Gifford (groin), LB Garret Wallow (hamstring), S Marques Sigle (ankle) OUT; WR Christian Kirk, CB Upton Stout (shoulder), S Siran Neal (knee) QUESTIONABLEFalcons: RB Brian Robinson (hamstring), OT Michael Jerrell (bicep), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) OUT; WR Beaux Collins (hip), WR Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), OT Cameron Williams (ankle), DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring), DE Za'Darius Smith (neck), DT Gervon Dexter (hamstring), LB Kendal Daniels (neck), CB C.J. Henderson (groin), CB A.J. Terrell (groin), CB Avieon Terrell (back) QUESTIONABLESan Francisco is looking to stay perfect this week, but once again has the weight of significant injuries hindering it. The offense will be without two top wide receivers, with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both ruled out ahead of the matchup. This is the second straight missed game for Samuel. As expected DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf) is also out. DL Mykel Williams (knee), who was sidelined to start the year, did not have a game designation this week after being upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a full participant on Friday.The Falcons have a lengthy injury report this week, ruling out four players, including RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm). With Deablo out, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable, could get the nod. CB A.J. Terrell (groin) and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) could make their return this week. Terrell spent the last four weeks on IR. Bengals vs. Ravens (-3)Bengals: No injury designations.Ravens: QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) OLB Tavius Robinson (pectoral), S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) OUT; CB T.J. Tampa (knee) DOUBTFUL; DT Broderick Washington (ankle) QUESTIONABLEOnly four Bengals players landed on the injury report this week. The three players who did not practice on Friday, DT Jonathan Allen, DT B.J. Hill and DT Dexter Lawrence, were all listed as "not injury related, rest."
QB Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, was initially listed as questionable for Week7 after being limited throughout the week of practice. However, the Ravens downgraded their start quarterback to out on Saturday, meaning he will miss his third-straight game. Tyler Huntley will get the start. Buccaneers vs. Panthers (-3.5)Buccaneers: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) OUT; QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) QUESTIONABLEPanthers: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) OUT; OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) QUESTIONABLEThe biggest takeaway from the Buccaneers injury report is the possibility of a return from starting QB Baker Mayfield, who has been dealing with a right thumb injury. He's missed the last three games, and in his place, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has led the offense. If he does come back, he will be without WR Emeka Egbuka, who currently leads the team in receiving yards (240). On the other side of the ball, S Antoine Winfield will miss his second straight game. Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) was listed on the injury report, but doesn't get a game designation and was a full participant all week. OT Monroe Freeling (knee) and LB Bam Martin-Scott were full participants all week, but get the questionable stamp.
Giants vs. Texans (-10)Giants: LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder), CB Greg Newsome II (concussion) OUT; TE Theo Johnson (neck) DOUBTFUL; OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), OL Marcus Mbow (knee), CB Paulson Adebo (knee), S Jevon Holland (concussion), S Tyler Nubin (neck) QUESTIONABLE Texans: RB David Montgomery (groin), OT Blake Fisher (thumb), S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand), S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) OUT; WR Tank Dell (knee) QUESTIONABLEGiants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) is reportedly out for the year, but at minimum is sidelined for this week. CB Greg Newsome (concussion) joins him as the only other Giant ruled out ahead of the matchup. TE Theo Johnson is doubtful after not practicing on Friday. S Jevon Holland (concussion) and OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) were limited the last two days after both not participating on Wednesday.The Texans could get WR Tank Dell (knee), who hasn't played since 2024, back this week. He is questionable after being a full participant on Wednesday and Thursday. Among those already ruled out are S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) and RB David Montgomery (groin). Colts vs. Vikings (-6.5)Colts: WR Anthony Gould (concussion), TE Tyler Warren (groin), CB Sauce Gardner (calf) OUT; LB CJ Allen (ankle), LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), CB Justin Walley (knee), P Rigoberto Sanchez (right foot) QUESTIONABLEVikings: RB Jordan Mason (thumb) QUESTIONABLEThe Colts injury report was lengthy this week. CB Sauce Gardner (calf) is out after suffering the injury in last week's loss. He did not practice all week. Tyler Warren (groin), who leads the team in receptions among TEs, is also out. CB Justin Walley (knee) didn't practice Wednesday and was limited the rest of the week. LB CJ Allen (ankle) and LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) were both non-participants on Friday.
Minnesota's injury report is very short this week, with just one player carrying a game designation. RB Jordan Mason (thumb) was a full participant all week. WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited to start the week, but after two full practices, is cleared to play. WR Jordan Addison (hamstring) will make his return after missing one week and getting extra time to rest during last week's bye. TE T.J. Hockenson is another who took full advantage of the rest, passing the concussion protocol and ruled good to go for this week.Dolphins vs. Jets (-4.5)Dolphins: CB Reese Taylor (quad) OUT; EDGE Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) DOUBTFUL; LB Willie Gay Jr. (illness), S Kyle Louis (knee) QUESTIONABLEJets: OL Max Mitchell (concussion), EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), LB Francisco Mauigoa (quad) OUT; RB Breece Hall (quad), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee), OL Dylan Parham (knee) QUESTIONABLEMiami has one player ruled out ahead of the divisional matchup, as they look to get their first win of the year. LB Willie Gay (illness) is questionable and was limited in practice on Friday. S Kyle Louis (knee) was a full participant on Friday after being limited the rest of the week. Jets RB Breece Hall, who has missed multiple weeks with a quad injury, could return to the offense this week. He was limited in practice over the last two days, an improvement over Wednesday's practice, when he was sidelined. The RB is officially questionable. EDGE Joseph Ossai remains out, missing his third straught game.
Browns (-1.5) vs. TitansBrowns: QB Dillon Gabriel (back), G Teven Jenkins (back), DT Khalil Davis (quad), DT Mike Hall (ankle) OUT; RB Dylan Sampson (knee), LB Quincy Williams (neck), CB Denzel Ward (hand), S Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) QUESTIONABLETitans: RB Tyjae Spears (knee), WR Calvin Ridley (hip), LB Dorian Mausi (foot), S Tony Adams (ankle), S Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) QUESTIONABLEThe Browns have a lengthy injury report this week with three players out, including DT Khalil Davis (quad) and G Teven Jenkins (back). CB Denzel Ward (hand) popped up in the injury report as limited on Friday and officially questionable. S Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) was limited the last two days after not participating on Wednesday.The Titans did not rule out any players ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, and five players are listed as questionable. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing the next two days. RB Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Friday. Safties Tony Adams (ankle) and Kevin Winston (quad) were both limited the first two days of the week and ended as full participants.Broncos (-4.5) vs. CardinalsBroncos: RB Tyler Badie (thumb), OLB Jonah Elliss (ankle), S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) OUT; RB Jonah Coleman (ankle), CB Patrick Surtain II (ankle) QUESTIONABLECardinals: RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), OL Jon Gaines II (knee/ankle), DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee) OUT; QB Carson Beck (back), DL Darius Robinson (back), CB Max Melton (knee), S Budda Baker (groin/illness) QUESTIONABLEThe Broncos will once again be without S Talanoa Hufanga, who suffered an ankle injury in Week 5. Denver has a few players who could return after missing multiple games. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) is questionable and was limited in practice this week, after missing the last two games. RB Jonah Coleman could make his return from IR and was a full participant all week. 
The Cardinals are dealing with numerous injuries this week. S Budda Baker played through injury in their Week 6 matchup but missed two days of practice before he was upgraded to limited on Friday. Another questionable player is CB Max Melton (knee), who did not practice the last two weeks. RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who leads the team in rushing, will be out this week. Packers vs. Lions (-3)Packers: LB Zaire Franklin (shin) OUT; WR Bo Melton (back), G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) QUESTIONABLELions: C Cade Mays (wrist), S Brian Branch (Achilles) QUESTIONABLEPackers LB Zaire Franklin is out for only the second time in his nine-year career. Franklin suffered the injury during Thursday's practice. DT Jordon Riley (Achilles) is on the PUP list and could make his return this week, after being limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. QB Jordan Love (back) and WR Christian Watson (ankle) were both on the injury report this week, but carry no game designations. The Lions have a short report this Friday. Just two players, C Cade Mays (wrist) and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are both questionable after full week's of practice. The only other player to land on the injury report this week was CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring), who was a full participant on Friday and doesn't carry a game designation.
Rams (-4.5) vs. RaidersRams: LB Nate Landman (concussion) OUT; WR Puka Nacua (calf), CB Trent McDuffie (groin) QUESTIONABLERaiders: WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring), TE Carter Runyon (foot) OUT; RB Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) QUESTIONABLEThe Rams could be without WR Puka Nacua (calf), who already missed two games this week. CB Trent McDuffie (groin), missed last week and is officially questionable, despite not practicing all week. The Rams are struggling at 2-4 and can use all the help they can get as they look to turn their season around. The Raiders ruled two players out, WR Dont'e Thornton (hamstring) and TE Carter Runyon (foot) ahead of Sunday's matchup. The Raiders, who have the fourth-fewest rushing yards by any offense in the league, could be without RB Washington (foot/back), who is questionable. Washington, who has the second-most rushing yards on the team, did not practice the last two days. TE Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited on Wednesday, but was back in full gear the rest of the week. Chiefs vs. Seahawks (-2.5)Chiefs: RB Brashard Smith (hamstring), WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), OL Jaylon Moore (concussion) OUT; LB Cooper McDonald (knee), CB L'Jarius Sneed (knee) QUESTIONABLESeahawks: RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), LB Chazz Surratt (calf), LB Drake Thomas (ankle) OUT; QB Drew Lock (right elbow), LB Demarcus Lawrence (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip), LB Connor O'Toole (hamstring), S Nick Emmanwori (hip) QUESTIONABLEThe Chiefs offense will be without RB Brashard Smith (hamstring), who was downgraded from limited Thursday to a non-participant on Friday. They will also be without WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) for the second week in a row. CB L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited all week and is questionable. TE Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited all week but carries no game designation. QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was also on the injury report but was at full capacity in practice all week. 
Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip) popped up on the injury report as a limited participant in Friday's practice and carries a questionable status. QB Drew Lock (right elbow), LB Demarcus Lawrence (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip), LB Connor O'Toole (hamstring) were all also limited on Friday and are questionable.Cowboys (-4.5) at Eagles (Monday)Cowboys: OT Drew Shelton (hamstring), WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs), LB Dee Winters (calf) OUT; OLB Marist Liufau (forearm), S P.J. Locke (foot) QUESTIONABLEEagles: DB Michael Carter (abdomen), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), OLB Nolan Smith (concussion), WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) OUT: RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle), EDGE Jalyx Hunt (knee, ankle), CB Jakorian Bennett (knee), TE Grant Calcaterra (back), G Landon Dickerson (knee, pectoral), TE Eli Stowers (quad) QUESTIONABLE. After starting the week off on a limited basis due to a shoulder injury, receiver George Pickens logged back-to-back full practices on Friday and Saturday and has no injury designation for Monday's matchup with Philly. Corner Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), left tackle Tyler Guyton (calf), linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) and corner Cobie Durant (hamstring) are also good to go. After not practicing at all this week, the Eagles have ruled out receiver DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury. The receiver room will be even more depleted with Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also sidelined for this game. On a more positive note, running back Saquon Barkley was upgraded to a full participant during Saturday's practice, signaling he is trending in the right direction despite the questionable designation.
